gaps.construct: nine parameters defaulting to None (tzinfo to True), fold keyword-only; callers write d.replace(day=1)
gaps.description: No defaults and no keyword arguments, so every call must pass nine positional values, mostly 'nothing'; this destroys the purpose of replace, which is to name only the fields that change.

gaps.construct: type(self)(...) constructs an instance of the receiver's own subclass
gaps.description: No self, no subclasses and no way to say 'build a value of the same type as this one'; the result is always a plain DateTime, so subclasses lose their type.

gaps.construct: tzinfo=True sentinel: True keeps, None clears, a value sets
gaps.description: maybe has two states, but the original needs three; a three-variant choice TzinfoChange is declared, which changes the caller's spelling.

gaps.construct: if x is None: x = self.x, repeated nine times
gaps.description: There is no 'value of a maybe, or else this default' expression outside together's 'or else none'; each field needs a var plus a four-line choose, turning 18 lines into about 45.

gaps.construct: a branch where nothing happens (keep the old value)
gaps.description: choose requires every case, and there is no 'do nothing' statement; whether a when branch containing only a note is valid is not stated.

gaps.construct: a broken-down local datetime with fold and optional tzinfo
gaps.description: The doc offers 'instant' and 'calendar date' as distinct types but no naive or zoned wall-clock date-time with a fold flag, so a plain record of Ints is used.

invented_syntax: to replace self year month ... (nine bare positional parameters with no label words)
notes: Optional keyword arguments with defaults are the whole interface of this function, and Scribe has no answer; a record-update form ('self with day 1') would solve this case and many like it. The nine-fold choose repetition is the clearest density-budget failure in my set. The doc's 'or else' wording in example 37 suggests a natural spelling for maybe defaults if it were made general.
